SMTO-EXE-0061 — SMTO can't move or resize the window to that spot

GUID: 353e7214-0e4e-5258-8837-702b24bb48ab
Slug: desktop-invalid-geometry
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • The position or size asked for would put the window off every screen, or the window is in full-screen mode, which can't be moved or resized. The window was left as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO for the window's current position and size, for example "where is that window and how big is it?". Knowing where it is now makes it easy to choose a spot that stays on screen.
  2. Ask again with a new position and size that keep at least part of the window on one of the screens. A window placed entirely off-screen couldn't be reached, so SMTO refuses it.
  3. If the window is in full-screen mode, leave full-screen mode by hand on that computer first, then ask again. Full-screen windows can't be moved or resized until they return to normal.

What success looks like

  • The window appears at the new position and size on that computer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer, with the position and size you asked for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Move/resize validation rejected geometry that does not intersect any known display, or the Linux/macOS target window is fullscreen and ineligible for that operation.

What this means

  • Move/resize validation found geometry that did not intersect a known display, or the Linux/macOS target was fullscreen and ineligible for that operation. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Move/resize validation found geometry that did not intersect a known display, or the Linux/macOS target was fullscreen and ineligible for that operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current coordinate space, display bounds and fullscreen state before choosing dimensions.

How to fix it

  • Read the window's current bounds and display coordinate space with desktop.windows, then send positive width/height whose rectangle intersects a known display (negative virtual-desktop coordinates are valid if they intersect). On Linux/macOS exit fullscreen first, then confirm the resulting bounds.
  • Inspect displays and window state; use valid positive bounds intersecting a display and leave fullscreen through a supported action when required.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the current window and display coordinate space, then use positive dimensions intersecting a known display.

How to verify the fix

  • Valid geometry is applied to the intended eligible window and its resulting bounds are observed.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
